nri-world.nri_angle: Central and Eastern Europe is emerging as an unexpected new frontier for the Indian diaspora as labour-short manufacturing economies recruit Indian engineers and technicians. Modi's first-ever visit signals New Delhi is tracking even the diaspora's smallest, fastest-growing outposts.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Students Are Fleeing Canada — Departures Fell 41 Percent in a Year. The Diaspora's Map Is Being Redrawn.
nri-world.excerpt: Official Indian government data shows the sharpest reversal in any major destination, as the Anglophone world tightens its doors and Germany, Ireland and the Gulf rise to take its place.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian student departures to Canada fell 41 percent (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Student migration is the leading edge of diaspora formation — the places that capture today's students host tomorrow's settled communities. The 2024 collapse in Canada, US, UK and Australia, paired with surges into Germany and the Gulf, signals where the Indian diaspora's next generation will take root.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: An India-US Trade Deal Is Suddenly Close. The US Trade Chief Visits This Month to Seal the First Tranche.
markets-finance.excerpt: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer travels to New Delhi on June 23-24 to put final touches on an interim agreement, with India's commerce minister signaling the first tranche could be done by mid-July. With a US-Iran truce cooling oil and the World Bank lifting its growth forecast, the macro backdrop has rarely looked better.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who said the first tranche of an India-US trade deal could be concluded by mid-July
markets-finance.nri_angle: An India-US trade pact sits at the center of the diaspora's two worlds — it shapes the export sectors and equities many NRIs invest in, the rupee that governs how far their remittances stretch, and the broader US-India relationship that frames diaspora life in America.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Defence Production Hits a Record ₹1.78 Lakh Crore — and the Stocks Riding the Boom Just Surged
markets-finance.excerpt: Government data shows India's annual defence output jumped 15.6 percent to an all-time high, with exports leaping 62 percent to nearly ₹38,500 crore and the private sector's share at a record. The Nifty India Defence index rose 3.9 percent as investors bet the 'Make in India' arms push has real momentum.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's defence production hit a record in FY26; the Nifty India Defence index surged 3.9 percent as exports jumped 62 percent
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's defence-manufacturing boom has become one of the most-watched investment themes for NRIs seeking exposure to the country's industrial rise — a story of self-reliance and export ambition that resonates with diaspora investors looking beyond IT and banks for the next structural growth story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Fed Just Stopped Promising Rate Cuts — and Started Hinting at a Hike. Warsh's First Meeting Spooked Wall Street.
markets-finance.excerpt: In Kevin Warsh's debut as Federal Reserve Chair, the central bank held rates at 3.50–3.75% but flipped its dot plot from an implied cut to an implied hike, sending US stocks sliding and the dollar firmer. For NRIs, a hawkish Fed reshapes everything from the rupee to mortgage rates to the calculus on sending money home.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Federal Reserve in Washington; the Fed held rates but flipped its projections toward a hike at Kevin Warsh's first meeting
markets-finance.nri_angle: A hawkish US Fed keeps the dollar strong and US mortgage and savings rates elevated — directly shaping how much NRIs earn on dollar deposits, what they pay on American home loans, and how many rupees their remittances buy back home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Markets Just Logged Their Longest Winning Streak in Two Months. The Engine Is Cheaper Oil — and a Fragile Iran Deal.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nifty 50 closed above 24,000 for the first time in weeks as benchmarks rose for a fourth straight session, riding a near-three-month low in crude after a US-Iran peace deal promised to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. For NRIs, falling oil is rocket fuel for the rupee and the inflation outlook — but the truce is far from sealed.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; India's benchmarks logged their longest winning run in two months as oil eased
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs, this rally is a three-way win and a warning at once — cheaper oil eases India's import bill and supports the rupee that governs every remittance, while the fragility of the Iran truce means the gains rest on a deal that could still unravel.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: AI Fear Gutted India's IT Stocks by 27%. Now Some of the World's Biggest Investors Are Calling It a Bargain.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has been hammered as investors bet that artificial intelligence will hollow out India's software outsourcing giants. But with BlackRock and others arguing the market has been 'over-punished,' the very sector everyone is fleeing is starting to look like the contrarian call of 2026.
markets-finance.image_caption: A Tata Consultancy Services building; India's IT index has fallen about 27% in 2026 on AI-disruption fears
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's IT giants are the bedrock of countless NRI portfolios and the employers of a generation of diaspora engineers — so the question of whether AI is a death sentence or an overblown panic for TCS, Infosys and Wipro is both a financial and a deeply personal one for Indian software professionals abroad.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: After a Record $30 Billion Exodus, Foreign Money Is Edging Back Into India. The Tide May Be Turning.
markets-finance.excerpt: Foreign investors yanked a record $30.8 billion out of Indian equities in 2026 — then turned net buyers for the first time in 13 sessions as a US-Iran peace deal cooled oil and the RBI moved to steady the rupee. Wall Street firms now say India was 'over-punished,' and its absence from the AI trade may finally be an advantage.
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock market display; foreign investors edged back into Indian equities this week
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs who watched Indian equities and their rupee-denominated portfolios slide through a brutal first half of 2026, the early signs of a foreign-money reversal reframe the question from 'how much more will I lose?' to whether the worst is now behind — and whether the diaspora's home-country bias is, for once, the contrarian call.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Biggest IPO Ever Is About to Land. Reliance Jio May File Draft Papers Within Days.
markets-finance.excerpt: Reliance Jio Infocomm could file draft papers for its expected $4 billion IPO within days — just before Mukesh Ambani's closely watched annual address on Friday — in what would be the first listing from his conglomerate in over two decades and potentially the largest public offering in Indian history.
markets-finance.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, whose Reliance Jio may file for India's largest-ever IPO within days
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio is the network most NRIs hand their relatives in India and the app bundle that powers their parents' digital lives; now the diaspora can weigh whether to own a slice of it — a decision sharpened by a record-breaking float that some veteran analysts warn has historically marked market tops.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Rupee Just Hit a Five-Week High and May Climb to 92. For NRIs Sending Money Home, the Window Is Closing.
markets-finance.excerpt: A US–Iran peace deal knocked oil prices to a three-month low and, stacked on the RBI's June measures to pull in dollars, sent the rupee surging for a third straight session to 94.56. One forecaster sees 92 per dollar by September. A stronger rupee is good news for India — but it means every dollar an NRI remits buys fewer rupees.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes; the currency hit a five-week high this week with forecasts of further gains
markets-finance.nri_angle: The rupee's direction is the single biggest variable in how much value an NRI's remittance or home-bound investment delivers — and with the currency now appreciating after months of weakness, the diaspora faces a narrowing window in which dollars still convert at favourable rates, a timing decision worth real money for anyone sending funds to family, servicing a loan, or funding property in India.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Bonds Are on the Cusp of Joining a Global Index That Moves Billions. The Review Lands This Month.
markets-finance.excerpt: After scrapping bond taxes and reopening the debt door, India is making its strongest bid yet for inclusion in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index — a move that could pull $20-25 billion into the country. For NRIs, it is a quiet but consequential signal.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, at the centre of the bond-market reforms
markets-finance.nri_angle: Index inclusion would steady the rupee, lift Indian bond holdings, and stamp global approval on India's fiscal management — all of which shape how NRIs remit, invest, and anchor portfolios to India.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: NRIs Are Quietly Paying Tax They May Not Owe on Indian Mutual Funds. A Treaty Clause Can Erase It.
markets-finance.excerpt: Fund houses deduct tax at source on NRI mutual-fund gains — up to 20 per cent on short-term equity profits — but a string of tribunal rulings has confirmed that NRIs in countries like the UAE and Singapore can invoke their Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement and owe India nothing on those capital gains. The catch: you have to claim it, and most do not.
markets-finance.image_caption: Mutual-fund and tax paperwork; NRIs in treaty-favourable countries can reclaim tax withheld on fund gains
markets-finance.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs hold Indian mutual funds and silently accept 12.5–20 per cent tax deducted at source on their gains — yet those living in treaty-favourable jurisdictions like the UAE, Singapore and others may legally owe India zero, meaning the difference is real money the diaspora can reclaim simply by understanding and asserting their DTAA rights.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Built a Tax-Light Financial City to Lure NRI Money Home. In 2026, GIFT City Is Finally Pulling.
markets-finance.excerpt: Once dismissed as a policy experiment, the GIFT City IFSC in Gujarat has become one of 2026's most talked-about destinations for NRI investments, India-focused funds and cross-border wealth structuring — offering a progressive regulatory regime and attractive tax incentives. But for all the momentum, its liquidity and depth still trail established hubs like Dubai and Singapore.
markets-finance.image_caption: The skyline of GIFT City, India's International Financial Services Centre in Gujarat
markets-finance.nri_angle: GIFT City is being engineered specifically as the on-ramp for NRI and OCI capital into India — a tax-efficient, dollar-friendly gateway that lets the diaspora invest in India-linked assets without routing through Dubai or Singapore — making the practical question of whether it is ready yet a direct, money-on-the-table decision for globally mobile Indians.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Banks Just Doubled Dollar Deposit Rates for NRIs to 7%. The RBI Engineered It — and It Will Not Last.
markets-finance.excerpt: After the RBI agreed on June 5 to absorb the full hedging cost on fresh three-to-five-year FCNR(B) dollar deposits, banks have lifted rates from around 3 per cent to between 5.25 and 7.1 per cent. With no currency risk, these are among the most attractive dollar-denominated returns NRIs have seen in years — but the concessional window slams shut on September 30, and the offer is dollar-only.
markets-finance.image_caption: US dollar banknotes; Indian banks are offering NRIs up to 7.1 per cent on dollar FCNR(B) deposits
markets-finance.nri_angle: FCNR(B) deposits are an NRI-only instrument, and the sudden jump to 6-7.1 per cent on a dollar deposit with zero currency risk — deliberately engineered by the RBI to pull diaspora dollars into India — is one of the most consequential, time-limited financial decisions facing NRI savers right now, with a hard September 30 deadline.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Beat Carlsen Twice and the World Champion Once. In Oslo, a 20-Year-Old From Chennai Showed Why India Now Runs Chess.
sports.excerpt: R Praggnanandhaa's Norway Chess title is the latest sign of a generational shift: a country that had one world champion in 2013 now has the reigning world champion, the tournament's winner, and a clutch of 2700-rated players barely out of their teens. For a global game increasingly played in Indian living rooms, the future has an accent.
sports.image_caption: R Praggnanandhaa, who won Norway Chess 2026 ahead of Magnus Carlsen and world champion Gukesh Dommaraju
sports.nri_angle: India's chess surge runs straight through diaspora living rooms — the same low-cost, high-prestige game that Indian-American and Indian-British families have embraced en masse is now producing the world's most exciting young grandmasters, making players like Praggnanandhaa and Gukesh proof of concept for a particular immigrant bet.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two Indian Teenagers Are One Win From a Wimbledon Junior Main Draw. A Decade Ago, This Was Unthinkable.
sports.excerpt: Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, seeded No. 1 in girls' qualifying, and 17-year-old Hitesh Chauhan both reached the final qualifying round at Roehampton — backed by academy training and corporate money that earlier generations never had.
sports.image_caption: The National Tennis Centre at Roehampton, the venue where Wimbledon junior qualifying is played

sports.nri_angle: The junior tennis pipeline India's rising players climb runs through the US college and ITF circuits where much of the diaspora lives, making these teenagers' breakthroughs personal and aspirational for Indian-American families.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: From a Bakersfield Muni to Shinnecock: The Gujarati-American Who Skipped Med School and Became the First IGPL Golfer at a Major
sports.excerpt: Manav Shah was supposed to be a doctor. Instead, the California-born son of Gujarati immigrants ground his way through Latin American mini-tours, rebuilt his game on an Indian circuit during a chance detour, and survived golf's toughest qualifier to reach the U.S. Open.
sports.image_caption: The first tee at Shinnecock Hills during the U.S. Open, where Manav Shah makes his Major debut
sports.nri_angle: Manav Shah is the immigrant-family story in miniature — a California-born son of Gujarati parents who chose golf over the expected path into medicine, kept his heritage alive through an Indian league, and now becomes the first IGPL golfer at a Major, a marker of how deep diaspora golf has grown.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Four Days After a Super Over Meltdown, India A Answered With 319 and a 101-Run Rout to Reach the Final
sports.excerpt: Three fifties — Tilak Varma's 59, plus 58 each from Priyansh Arya and Kumar Kushagra — and Nishant Sindhu's 4/31 carried India A into the tri-series final in Dambulla. It is the same A-team shop window that has been quietly minting India's senior internationals.
sports.image_caption: India A captain Tilak Varma, who top-scored with 59 as India A reached the tri-series final in Dambulla
sports.nri_angle: NRIs follow India's senior XI obsessively, but the A-team in Dambulla is where the next Gill or Jaiswal is being forged — the names on this team sheet are the players the diaspora will be watching for India over the next decade.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Same Week the Men Finished Last, India's Women Are Unbeaten in Auckland — and One Step From a Pro League Promotion
sports.excerpt: India's women's hockey team beat the USA 3-2 from two goals down, then edged Japan 2-1 to reach the FIH Nations Cup semi-finals with a game to spare. Win the tournament in New Zealand and they are promoted to the 2026-27 FIH Pro League — the elite circuit the men's side just endured a winless season in.
sports.image_caption: India captain Salima Tete, who scored against Japan as India reached the FIH Women's Nations Cup semi-finals in Auckland
sports.nri_angle: Hockey carries deep heritage for Indians abroad, and a Nations Cup win would promote India's women — led by athletes from Jharkhand's Simdega belt and the northeast — to the elite FIH Pro League, putting them on the same broadcast calendars the diaspora already follows for cricket and football.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Just Posted Their Highest-Ever World Cup Total. Mandhana and Shafali Took 11 Overs to Bury the Netherlands.
sports.excerpt: Smriti Mandhana (74 off 47) and Shafali Verma (55 off 38) shared a 115-run opening stand and brought up India's joint-fastest team fifty in Women's T20 World Cup history. India's 209 for 5 at Headingley was the most they have ever made at a World Cup — and a debutant Netherlands side never stood a chance.
sports.image_caption: Smriti Mandhana, who top-scored with 74 off 47 balls as India posted their highest-ever Women's T20 World Cup total
sports.nri_angle: India's women have never won a senior global title, and a generation of NRI families in Britain has watched them grow into genuine contenders — Headingley, in the heart of Yorkshire's South Asian community, drew a vocal, flag-waving diaspora crowd.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two Centuries, a 224-Run Stand, and India's 500th ODI Win: Gill and Kishan Sink Afghanistan in Lucknow
sports.excerpt: Shubman Gill's ninth ODI hundred and Ishan Kishan's maiden century carried India to a 15-run victory at Lucknow, sealing the three-match series 2-0 with a game to spare — and handing the country a landmark 500th win in one-day internationals.
sports.image_caption: Shubman Gill scored his ninth ODI century to lead India past Afghanistan in the second ODI at Lucknow
sports.nri_angle: India's white-ball rebuild under captain Shubman Gill is appointment viewing for the cricket-following Indian diaspora, and a milestone 500th ODI win, twin centuries, and a touch of old-fashioned sportsmanship make for exactly the kind of storyline NRIs forward to family group chats within minutes.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: 274 Days Without a Throw. On Friday, Neeraj Chopra Finally Returns — in the City Where He First Broke 90 Metres.
sports.excerpt: India's two-time Olympic javelin medallist will open his 2026 season at the Doha Diamond League on June 19, his first competition since a back injury wrecked his World Championships last September. He walks into a nine-man field led by a Sri Lankan who has already thrown 92.62m this year.
sports.image_caption: Neeraj Chopra, India's two-time Olympic javelin medallist, returns at the Doha Diamond League on June 19
sports.nri_angle: Neeraj Chopra is India's most globally followed track-and-field athlete — the man who ended a 100-year wait for Olympic athletics gold — and NRIs across the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf treat his competitions as appointment viewing, often setting alarms for awkward hours to watch a single throw.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Nine Games, Zero Wins: India's Hockey Team Is Having Its Worst Pro League Ever — at the Worst Possible Time
sports.excerpt: India sit eighth of nine in the FIH Pro League with four points and a minus-17 goal difference, having not won a single match in regulation. With the World Cup and Asian Games months away, Craig Fulton's side faces Germany in Rotterdam needing to prove the slump is a blip, not a warning.
sports.image_caption: India captain Harmanpreet Singh receiving the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award; his side is enduring a winless 2025-26 FIH Pro League campaign
sports.nri_angle: Hockey is India's national sport by heritage, and NRIs across the US, UK, Canada and Australia follow the Pro League on Star Sports and JioHotstar. A winless campaign just as India should be peaking for the World Cup and Asian Games lands hard with a diaspora that treats the team's revival as a point of pride.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A 21-Year-Old From Madurai Just Won an NCAA Title in Eugene. It Was India's First in Four Years.
sports.excerpt: Selva Prabhu leapt 16.92m at Hayward Field to take the 2026 NCAA Outdoor triple jump crown for Kansas State — India's first NCAA outdoor athletics title since Tejaswin Shankar in 2022, and the latest proof that the American college system has become a real pathway for Indian track and field.
sports.image_caption: Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon, where Selva Prabhu won the 2026 NCAA Outdoor triple jump title for Kansas State
sports.nri_angle: Selva Prabhu's NCAA title shows how the American college system has become a real development pathway for Indian track-and-field talent — a pipeline diaspora families already know intimately, now producing national champions.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A Month After the First Indian-Heritage Major Champion, the U.S. Open Has Its Deepest-Ever Diaspora Field
sports.excerpt: Aaron Rai arrives at Shinnecock Hills as a major winner, Akshay Bhatia as a ranked contender, and two qualifiers complete the largest contingent of golfers of Indian origin the championship has ever seen.

sports.title: She Outranked Kohli and Rohit on a List Headlined by LeBron. Smriti Mandhana Is the Only Indian on TIME's 100 Most Influential in Sports.

technology.title: eBay Is Cutting 639 American Jobs While Filing for 429 H-1B Workers. Indians Will Wear the Backlash.
technology.excerpt: The e-commerce firm's own filings put layoffs and visa applications side by side — handing Washington exactly the ammunition it has been hunting for.
technology.image_caption: eBay's Silicon Valley headquarters in San Jose, California
technology.nri_angle: Indians get ~70% of H-1B visas, so when a company lays off Americans while filing for foreign workers, Indian professionals become the lightning rod in a political fight over corporate cost-cutting and AI automation.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Microsoft Just Shipped an AI That Finishes Your Work, Not Drafts It. Satya Nadella Warns It Could Hollow Out Industries.
technology.excerpt: Copilot Cowork goes global the same week its own CEO cautions that a few AI models could 'eat everything they see' — and Indian tech workers sit on both sides of that bet.
technology.nri_angle: Cowork automates the multi-step office workflows that employ hundreds of thousands of Indians at firms like TCS and Cognizant, making Nadella's 'move up the stack' warning a direct career instruction for the diaspora.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Accenture Reports Earnings Under an AI Cloud. The Company That Employs the Most Indians Is a Referendum on the Whole Sector.
technology.excerpt: Wall Street wants to know whether a business built on selling human hours can survive when the hours go machine-supplied — and lakhs of Indian careers ride on the answer.
technology.image_caption: Accenture's office building in Gachibowli, Hyderabad
technology.nri_angle: Accenture's largest employee base is in India and its US ops run heavily on Indian H-1B/L-1 talent, so its earnings double as a verdict on whether AI is hollowing out the mid-career IT jobs the diaspora climbed toward.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Satya Nadella Has a New Word for the AI Age: 'Token Capital.' It's a Warning Dressed as a Buzzword.
technology.excerpt: Microsoft's CEO says the winners won't own the smartest model — they'll own the learning loop. For India's engineers and IT giants, that reframes the whole AI threat.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, who introduced the 'token capital' framework at Build 2026
technology.nri_angle: Nadella's 'token capital' framing recasts AI as a chance for India's IT majors and the diaspora's engineers to own institutional knowledge rather than be commoditised by it — a counter-narrative to the AI-layoff panic.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Adobe Beat Earnings and Hit a 7-Year Low. The CFO Left for a Chip Company. That Tells You Everything.
technology.excerpt: Shantanu Narayen's Adobe tripled its AI revenue and raised guidance — then watched its stock crater on a double leadership vacuum and a deeper fear about software's future.
technology.image_caption: Shantanu Narayen, Adobe's chief executive of 18 years, who has announced he will step down once a successor is named
technology.nri_angle: Adobe's stumble matters to the diaspora: Narayen is among the longest-serving Indian-origin Silicon Valley CEOs, and the firm's large India engineering base and H-1B staff are exposed to the strategic uncertainty now hanging over the company.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Biggest Brokerages Just Got Cleared to Sell You Apple and Nvidia. The Gateway Is a City in Gujarat.
technology.excerpt: Zerodha, Groww, Angel One and Upstox have IFSCA approval to offer direct US-stock access through GIFT City — collapsing the wall between Indian retail savers and Wall Street.
technology.image_caption: The GIFT One tower in Gujarat's GIFT City, the finance hub serving as the gateway for Indians to buy U.S. stocks (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: A cheaper, regulated channel for Indians to buy US stocks deepens the financial bridge NRIs straddle daily — and ties the Indian middle class directly to the Silicon Valley fortunes the diaspora helps build.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Zepto Wants to Be India's First Pure Quick-Commerce IPO. The Valuation Tells the Real Story.
technology.excerpt: The ten-minute delivery giant filed to raise ₹8,010 crore at a reported $7 billion — below rival Swiggy. For NRI investors, July's listing is a referendum on the cash-burn era.
technology.image_caption: Zepto, the quick-commerce startup pursuing India's first pure 10-minute-delivery IPO (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Zepto is the cleanest available bet on a uniquely Indian behaviour NRIs watch family members do daily, and its listing will tell diaspora angel investors whether growth-at-any-cost is finally over.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Is Done Pretending It Will Ban Crypto. It Has a Bigger Plan: Owning the Money Itself.
technology.excerpt: Coinbase just switched on rupee trading while the RBI repositions the digital rupee as strategic infrastructure. For the diaspora, the real story is cheaper remittances — and far tighter surveillance.
technology.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India in Mumbai, which is building out the digital rupee as India pivots from banning crypto to issuing its own (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: A cross-border digital-rupee corridor could cut the cost of the $100B+ NRIs remit home each year, even as tighter KYC and geo-tagging make diaspora crypto moves fully visible and taxable.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Space Programme Is No Longer Just ISRO. For the Diaspora, That Changes the Bet.
technology.excerpt: A wave of state grants and $100 million in deep-tech deals signed in France point to a privatised space sector — and a new reason for NRI capital and engineers to look home.
technology.nri_angle: India's space story is shifting from a source of NRI pride to a source of NRI opportunity, with diaspora capital and returning engineers poised to fund the next generation of launch and Earth-observation startups.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The World's Cybersecurity Firms Are Quietly Moving to Bengaluru. India's Tech Job Map Is Being Redrawn.
technology.excerpt: As US visa fights make importing Indian engineers expensive, multinationals are building the jobs in India instead — and India's captive-center workforce is on track to hit 2.36 million this year.
technology.image_caption: Bengaluru, the city absorbing the bulk of India's new cybersecurity capability centers (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: For Indian engineers weighing whether the H-1B ladder is still worth climbing, the GCC boom signals that the best jobs at American firms may increasingly be in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, not Silicon Valley.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Startup Money Is Flowing Again — and This Week the Smart Capital Bet on Boring

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be Just What's in Ultra-Processed Foods That Hurts You — It's How They're Made
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new Tufts University analysis of two decades of US health data found that people who ate more ultra-processed foods had worse health and a higher risk of early death — even after accounting for the nutrition inside the food. The processing itself, the researchers argue, may carry an independent harm.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Packaged ultra-processed foods; a Tufts analysis found their industrial processing may harm health independent of the nutrition they contain
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian and South Asian families increasingly lean on packaged namkeen, instant mixes, sugary biscuits and ready meals as life gets busier abroad — and this research suggests the industrial processing in those products may damage health in ways that reading the nutrition label alone will never reveal.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Most Addictive Foods Aren't Only the Sugary Ones. A New Study Points the Finger at Refined Starch.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers analyzing why ultra-processed foods are so hard to stop eating found that the usual villain — sugar — is only half the story. Rapidly digested refined carbohydrates, even in savory snacks with little or no added sugar, may be just as powerful a driver of cravings.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Savory snacks like potato chips and fried namkeen deliver rapidly digested refined starch that researchers link to hard-to-stop cravings
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian snacking culture is built on refined-flour and rapidly-digested treats — namkeen, sev, mathri, fried maida snacks and white-rice indulgences — and this research suggests these savory staples may hijack appetite as effectively as anything sweet, a blind spot for a community already prone to diabetes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Cheap Amino-Acid Supplement Plus Exercise Cut Older Adults' Fatigue Almost in Half, a Pilot Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a controlled study of obese older adults, those who paired eight weeks of exercise with branched-chain amino acids saw fatigue fall 45 percent and depressive symptoms drop — while the placebo group's tiredness nearly doubled. The findings hint at a low-cost way to help aging bodies recover from the very exercise meant to keep them strong.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Older adults exercising; a UT Health San Antonio pilot trial found branched-chain amino acids cut fatigue 45 percent when paired with exercise
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many diaspora families care for aging parents who eat largely vegetarian diets that can fall short on the leucine-rich protein that guards against age-related muscle loss — making an affordable amino-acid strategy especially relevant for South Asian elders at high risk of sarcopenia and frailty.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Bad Sleep May Do More Than Tire You Out — A Study of 1.8 Million People Links Insomnia to an Irregular Heartbeat
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In one of the largest analyses of its kind, Japanese researchers found that people with insomnia had a 14 percent higher chance of developing atrial fibrillation, the irregular heart rhythm that raises the risk of stroke. The link was strongest in women and in adults under 65.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 1.8 million people linked insomnia to a 14 percent higher risk of atrial fibrillation, with the strongest effect in women and adults under 65
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry a well-documented double burden of disrupted sleep and early heart disease, and diaspora life adds its own insomnia triggers — late-night calls across time zones, shift work and chronic stress — making the sleep-heart connection especially worth heeding for the community.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Gut Microbe Helped People Keep the Weight Off. A New Trial Puts a Number on It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a randomized trial published in Nature Medicine, adults who took a daily dose of a pasteurized gut bacterium after dieting regained far less weight than those on a placebo — 2.6 pounds versus 7.1 — over six months. It is the clearest human evidence yet that the bug in your gut may decide whether the kilos stay off.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An illustration of gut microbiota; a Nature Medicine trial found a pasteurized gut bacterium cut weight regain by more than half
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians are uniquely prone to regaining weight as dangerous visceral fat after dieting, and to the early diabetes that follows — a microbiome-based tool that helps the weight stay off could matter more for the diaspora than for almost any other group.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The People You Live With Are Quietly Rewiring Your Gut. A New Study Maps How Microbes Spread Under One Roof.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers found that people who share a home share a quarter of their oral microbes — and romantic partners share far more — regardless of whether they eat the same food. The finding reframes health as something families pass between one another, microbe by microbe.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A family sharing a meal; new research finds people who live together share about a quarter of their oral microbes
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Multigenerational living — grandparents, parents and children under one roof — is a hallmark of diaspora households, which means the microbes, and the health risks and benefits they carry, are shared more intensely in Indian families than in the nuclear homes this kind of research usually studies.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Longevity Sweet Spot Is Not the Gym Rat's. Just 90 Minutes of Weights a Week Cut Death Risk in a 30-Year Study.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Harvard researchers followed nearly 150,000 adults for three decades and found that 90 to 119 minutes of strength training a week was the dose linked to the lowest risk of dying — from any cause, from heart disease and from brain disease. Pile on more and the benefit flattens. Pair it with cardio and it deepens.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person training with dumbbells; a 30-year study found 90 to 119 minutes of weekly strength work cut death risk most
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians lose muscle earlier and carry more dangerous visceral fat than most populations, yet weight training is still treated as vanity in many diaspora households — this 30-year study reframes a modest 90 minutes a week of resistance work as a longevity prescription, not gym vanity.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: You Do Not Need to Sit Less. You Need to Stand Up More Often. A New Trial Found Rising From Your Chair Lowers Blood Pressure.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A UC San Diego study put post-menopausal women through three months of small changes and found something counterintuitive: simply standing up more frequently — about 25 extra times a day — nudged down blood pressure, while merely sitting less did not deliver a clear win.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older woman rising from a chair; a UCSD trial found standing up more often lowered blood pressure
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora women, especially after menopause, carry an outsized burden of hypertension and heart disease that often goes under-treated — and this study offers a no-cost, no-equipment habit that fits the desk-bound, family-juggling reality of many Indian-American households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Skinny Jab Has a Hidden Catch. People on Ozempic Are Quietly Moving Less, Not More.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind study tracking the Fitbit data of more than 750 adults found that daily steps and exercise both fell after they started a GLP-1 weight-loss drug — the opposite of what most assume. Because these medicines also strip away muscle, doctors warn that moving is no longer optional.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen; a new study found activity fell after people started GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: GLP-1 jabs are sweeping through diaspora WhatsApp groups and family circles as the fix for the stubborn 'thin-fat' South Asian midriff — but this study warns that losing weight on the drug while moving less can shed the very muscle that protects against the community's early diabetes and heart disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Two-Year Brain Experiment Just Proved You Can Slow Mental Decline. The Recipe Is Boring — and It Works.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The landmark US POINTER trial put more than 2,000 at-risk older adults on a structured plan of exercise, the MIND diet, brain training and health check-ins. After two years, the group with the most structure and accountability showed measurably better thinking and memory than those left to do it alone.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Older adults exercising together; the US POINTER trial paired structured exercise with diet and brain training
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Dementia carries deep stigma and few answers in many Indian families, where ageing parents are cared for at home; this trial offers a low-cost, drug-free playbook — much of it built on movement, vegetables, lentils and community — that maps neatly onto how the diaspora already lives.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Five-a-Day May Not Be Enough for Your Heart. The Foods That Matter Most Are Hiding in Plain Sight.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of more than 30,000 adults in the US and UK found that even people who hit their fruit-and-vegetable targets rarely got enough flavanols — the plant compounds tied to a sharply lower risk of dying from heart disease. The fix is in specific foods: berries, apples with skin, beans and green tea.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Berries and green tea are among the richest sources of heart-protective flavanols
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The diaspora dutifully fills the fridge with fruit and vegetables, but a new analysis shows the heart benefit hinges on which ones — and several of the richest sources (apples, beans, the chai-adjacent habit of green tea) slot easily into an Indian kitchen already built around dal, sabzi and a daily cup.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Three Servings of Whole Grains a Day Kept the Waistline in Check for 18 Years. The Refined Stuff Did the Opposite.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking more than 3,100 adults for nearly two decades, researchers using data from one of the longest-running heart studies found that people who ate at least three daily servings of whole grains gained far less around the middle — and saw smaller rises in blood sugar and blood pressure — than those who leaned on refined grains.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Whole grains; a near-18-year study tied three daily servings to a slower-growing waistline
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The diaspora plate runs heavy on white rice and refined-flour rotis, naan and parathas — exactly the foods this 18-year study ties to a creeping waistline and rising blood sugar; swapping in brown rice, whole-wheat atta, millets and oats is a low-effort move against the abdominal fat that drives South Asian diabetes.
